=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (multiple images show leaves attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides, e.g., Image 2 and Image 3)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear grouped at the shoot tip in most views)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf blade is undivided)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or lobes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are widest below the middle and taper to a distinct tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tips taper to a slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (base tapers somewhat to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, pinnate, curving toward the apex
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaves have a glossy appearance reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are distinct but short relative to the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the visible stems appear green and flexible)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stems appear smooth)
    19. Stem color: green
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Some leaves show minor damage, such as small holes or missing margin fragments, but no cause is inferred.
